title: Maximum-linearity quadratic APN functions beyond dimension eight
summary: Decide whether a quadratic APN function can attain linearity $2^{n-1}$ in any even dimension greater than eight.

formal_statement.body: Does there exist an even integer $n>8$ and a quadratic APN function $F:\mathbb F_2^n\to\mathbb F_2^n$ such that $$\operatorname{Lin}(F)=\max_{a\in\mathbb F_2^n,\ b\in\mathbb F_2^n\setminus\{0\}}|W_F(a,b)|=2^{n-1}?$$ Construct one such pair $(n,F)$, or prove that no such function exists in any even dimension $n>8$.

scope.domain: Quadratic APN vectorial Boolean functions in even dimensions
assumptions: F : F_2^n -> F_2^n is quadratic and almost perfect nonlinear
Linearity is the maximum absolute component Walsh coefficient
scope.unresolved_remainder: The source constructs dimension-eight examples, but no quadratic APN function of linearity $2^{n-1}$ is known in any even dimension above eight and no global nonexistence theorem is known.

provenance.note: The source attributes the higher-dimensional question to Carlet, but the antecedent text available in this audit did not expose the complete residual quantifiers n > 8.

progress.summary: After constructing examples in dimension eight, the source states the exact residual existence question for even dimensions greater than eight.
